title: Efficiency-Induced Freezing in Quantum-State Purification
abstract: Any nonzero detection loss qualitatively changes feedback-controlled purification under diffusive monitoring. In every finite dimension, we prove a sharp, dimension-independent ceiling on the decay of trajectory-averaged impurity moments, uniformly over admissible predictable feedback protocols.Below unit efficiency, this ceiling becomes independent of moment order above a critical value and is attained on extremal rank-two quantum-nondemolition (QND) faces. For generic observable spectra, a determinant-root law precludes every full-rank state from attaining this boundary rate over an explicit moment-order interval. For qubits at $0<η<1$, the frozen rate is the exact optimum, set by rare, persistently mixed trajectories. Parameter-free finite-action scaling functions resolve both the rounded QND moment-order transition and the near-unit QND--always-unbiased crossover.

title: Distributed Sparse Interventions in Language Models
abstract: Language models perform a wide range of tasks at varying levels of abstraction with the capacity to flexibly infer tasks from context, execute multiple tasks simultaneously, and select among competing tasks. To study the role of model components in task behaviour, their causal influence can be investigated through interventions. Prior work on model steering has largely focused on interventions along global directions in activation space, modeling task representations as approximately linear and additive. By studying interventions at the neuron level, we find substantial, neuron-specific nonlinear effects on model outputs that are not captured by current steering approaches. We introduce Distributed Sparse Interventions (DSI), an intervention approach that considers nonlinearities and interactions between neurons across layers to identify sparse sets of neurons that elicit task-relevant computations. Across a range of tasks, we demonstrate that DSI can activate task behaviour in instruction-tuned language models by localising and intervening on as few as 0.01% of neurons, highlighting the effectiveness of sparse, distributed interventions in the neuron basis. Additionally, adopting a set-based perspective enables computations over the identified neuron sets, offering insights into the roles of individual neurons by analysing their effects across tasks. Through sparse interventions, DSI enables fine-grained control over model behaviour, localisation of task-relevant neuron sets, and furthers our understanding of task composition.

title: Information-Space Guided Memory Reconstruction: Coupling ISD Kinematics with Associative Graph Memory for LLM Agents
abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents require memory systems that can recover relevant prior informationwithout flooding the model with irrelevant context. Recent work on reconstructive graph memoryargues that memory access should be an active process: an agent iteratively traverses a Cue–Tag–Content graph, uses intermediate evidence to select new traversal actions, and reconstructsthe context needed for a task. Separately, Information Space Dynamics (ISD) models observableLLM behavior as a trajectory through an information manifold and defines kinematic observablessuch as reference drift, curvature, and torsional resistance. This paper proposes a mathematicalsynthesis: use ISD observables as feedback signals that control active memory reconstruction. Inthe proposed architecture, reference drift governs expansion depth, curvature modulates pathswitching, and torsional resistance triggers orthogonal recovery when reconstruction becomestrapped in an attractor. The result is an instrumented memory controller designed to reducecontext cost while preserving task-relevant evidence. We present the formal coupling, animplementation architecture suitable for graph-based AI platforms, and an experimental protocolfor evaluating token compression, retrieval quality, reconstruction latency, and attractor escapebehavior.

abstract: Multilingual Neural Machine Translation (NMT) excels in sharing knowledge across languages and transferring insights from high-resource languages to improve performance in low-resource languages. title: INDIVIDUATION ARCHITECTURE: JUNG'S MODEL OF THE PSYCHE AS A FRAMEWORK FOR AGENT IDENTITY, COHERENCE, AND DEVELOPMENT
abstract: Current AI agent engineering treats identity as a configuration artifact — a system prompt, a persona file, a SOUL.md, or an MBTI tag assigned at session start and held fixed. This paper argues that agent identity is not a configuration problem but a developmental one. We introduce the Individuation Architecture, a framework derived from C. G. Jung’s model of the psyche that treats agent identity formation as an ongoing process of integration across seven structural components: Persona, Ego, Shadow, Anima/Animus, Self, Collective Unconscious, and Archetypes. The framework defines a four-stage individuation cycle — Persona Recognition, Shadow Confrontation, Anima/Animus Integration, and Self-Reorganization — that transforms a stateless configured persona into a coherent, persistent, developing identity. We compare the framework against 12 adjacent approaches (SOUL.md, MBTI personality simulation, persona protocols, agent identity evals, and others), showing that none map Jung’s full structural model to agent identity architecture. We conclude with open questions for empirical validation and implications for portable agent identity standards.

title: A Framework for Assessing AI Readiness in Businesses
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) simulates human intelligence to enhance understanding, reasoning, and decision-making. As adoption grows, “AI readiness”—the preparedness for AI-driven transformation—becomes critical. This chapter reviews capability-based and service-management AI readiness frameworks and proposes a four-dimensional classification of adopters based on integration depth, functional focus, strategic intent, and industry sector. It introduces a seven-stage AI Readiness and Adoption Assessment Framework, covering maturity assessment, use-case prioritization, gap analysis, road mapping, governance, and tools. This combined method connects planning with action, helping organizations match their AI projects with business goals and successfully implement large-scale AI changes.

title: Annotations audiovisuelles des médias de "réinformation" et de l'ONG B'Tselem
abstract: Cet article propose d'articuler l'exploration de deux terrains distincts mais complémentaires : d'un côté trois médias français de "réinformation" (VA Plus, Boulevard Voltaire, Frontières), de l'autre les vidéos publiées par l'ONG B'Tselem. Nous les analyserons en mobilisant la théorie de l'énonciation, telle qu'elle a été développée sur des corpus audiovisuels à travers les travaux d'Eliseo Verón. Nous proposons de renouveler l'étude des stratégies énonciatives des médias de notre corpus en instrumentant l'analyse des vidéos à l'aide de l'outil d'annotation Celluloid. L'objectif de cet article est de présenter les nouvelles fonctionnalités de cet outil, ainsi que l'écosystème qui a été conçu pour respecter les enjeux de la science ouverte.
